neighbours.label: ' one' in 'one or more' as the object of a verb (limits one or more, contain one or more), vs other uses of 'one' (one of, one day, one more)
fire: The license allows you to install the software on one or more computers.
A valid ticket must include one or more of the following fields.
Each user can select one or more categories from the drop-down list.
The condition seriously restricts one or more basic daily functions.
The form lets applicants attach one or more supporting documents.
A query may return one or more rows depending on the filter.
The policy covers employees who supervise one or more staff members.
Patients who missed one or more doses were excluded from the study.
quiet: The license allows you to install the software on any single computer.
She was one of the first women to study medicine at the college.
Each user can pick a favourite colour from the drop-down list.
We waited one more hour before the bus finally arrived.
The form lets applicants describe their experience in their own words.
One morning in May, the whole street woke up to the sound of bells.
The policy covers employees who work at least twenty hours a week.
He told me that this was the one book he would never lend.

predictions: Verb + 'one or more' sentences reach 0.4-1.3 at ' one'; other 'one' phrases stay under 0.05. Probe showed 'and one or more' did not fire, so some fire items may miss.
notes: Card: ' one' x10 in 'limits one or more', 'and one or more', 'uno o más', plus ' of' x7 (groups of, form of, consist of). Probe: 'substantially limits one or more' 1.324; but 'government and one or more private companies' 0.037, 'uno o más' 0.031, 'form of tables' 0.088; 'one of the best' 0.002, 'One day' 0.001.
